_doc: HYPOTHETICAL track: 'CAN <PERSON> GET INTO <SCHOOL>?' for people who did NOT attend
that school. Sister file to celebs.json, which is the factual own-alma-mater track.
THE ACCURACY LINE, and it is not negotiable:
'achievement' and 'awards' are REAL, publicly documented accomplishments. They are
what gets fed to the engine as the extracurricular/spike signal, and they are the
only person-specific input.
'gpa' and 'sat' are INVENTED. Nobody's real academic record is known or claimed.
They MUST be shown on-slide as an explicit hypothetical ('if they applied with a
3.5 and a 1250'), never asserted as that person's stats. The title is a QUESTION
for the same reason -- it asserts nothing about anyone.
WHY THIS FORMAT WORKS NOW: the 2026-07-26 exceptional-EC fix means a world-class
achievement actually moves the number (a 3.4/1200 with an elite spike reads 7-18% at
Harvard instead of 1-2%). Before that fix every celeb would have returned the same
flat 1-2% and the format would have been dead on arrival.
The payoff question is the hook: does being the best on Earth at one thing beat
grades? Candor answers it on screen. Sometimes the answer is no, and that is the
more interesting carousel.
'academic_note' is the exact hypothetical wording for the stamp. Keep it plain.
Photos: static/celebs/<id>.jpg, optional -- missing degrades to logo-only cover.
PERISHABLE: category 'worldcup' entries were researched 2026-07-26, one week after
the 2026 World Cup final (Spain 1-0 Argentina, July 19, MetLife Stadium -- the
tournament was hosted in the US, so it is peak conversation here right now). Post
these FIRST; they go stale fastest. Re-verify before reusing them next season.
Everything in those entries is sourced from Wikipedia as of that date -- Rodri's
business administration degree from Jaume I University is real and documented, and
is the strongest hook in the file for that reason. Messi has NOT retired (contracted
to Inter Miami through 2028); do not write him as retiring.
